rows.name: DICE_LSF_RUNNING
rows.values: Only the exact text `1` counts. Any other text behaves like unset.
rows.default: Unset: the process counts as not started by `bin/dice-lsf-runner`.
rows.effect: Marks a process that `bin/dice-lsf-runner` started inside an LSF job. With `--remote`, the wrappers `bin/rinzler` and `bin/runtron` and `bin/slice` do not submit to LSF again and run locally. The wrappers and `bin/slice submit` reject an `--instance` option that differs from the `--instance` in `SYSTEM_CONFIG`.
rows.notes: Without `--instance` in `SYSTEM_CONFIG`, the accepted `--instance` is `0,1`. With `1`, `bin/slice run` does not move to a smaller slot range when FPGA cards are busy. With `mode: shared` in `/etc/positron/dice.yaml`, the Dice daemon rejects a request that has `1` and no `DICE_LSF_LEASE_PID`.

rows.name: DICE_LSF_TERMINAL_OUTPUT
rows.values: Only the exact text `1` counts. Any other text behaves like unset.
rows.default: Unset: `bin/slice run` draws its live status block only when stderr is a terminal.
rows.effect: `bin/slice run` draws its live status block with terminal control sequences even when stderr is not a terminal.
rows.notes: `bin/dice-lsf-runner` sets `1` when `bin/dice-lsf-submit` runs with `--wait` and its stdout is a terminal. Without the variable and without a terminal, `bin/slice run` under `DICE_LSF_RUNNING=1` prints at most one progress line every 10 seconds.

rows.name: DICE_NUMA_SIZES
rows.values: Positive integers separated by commas, one slot count per NUMA node in slot order, for example `4,4`. Parsed with `int`. The sum must equal the slot count of the server.
rows.default: Unset: the daemon derives the counts from `numa_nodes` in `config/resource-map.yaml`. If that fails, it treats the whole server as one NUMA node.
rows.effect: Tells the Dice daemon how many slots each NUMA node has. The daemon first looks for free adjacent slots inside one NUMA node. It uses slots that cross NUMA nodes only when no such block is free.
rows.notes: The daemon reads it once at startup. A value that does not parse, has a count below 1 slot, or has a wrong sum is not an error. The daemon then treats the whole server as one NUMA node and does not read `config/resource-map.yaml`.

rows.name: DICE_SLOTS
rows.values: Slot numbers joined by commas, for example `4,5,6,7`. `rinzler` and `runtron` reject spaces, empty items and ranges. The wrappers skip empty items. `bin/slice` also accepts ranges such as `4-7`.
rows.default: Unset: the process holds no Dice grant. `rinzler` and `runtron` fail at startup when `DICE_DAEMON_CHILD` is `1` and this variable is unset or empty.
rows.effect: Names the slots that Dice granted to the process. `rinzler` and `runtron` derive their instance from the slots. The wrappers `bin/rinzler` and `bin/runtron` confirm the grant with the Dice daemon, and `bin/slice run` uses the slots as its budget.
rows.notes: `rinzler` and `runtron` read it only when `DICE_DAEMON_CHILD` is `1`. The slots must then form one unbroken run that equals one `--instance` share. An `--instance` in `SYSTEM_CONFIG` that names other slots fails startup. The wrappers and `bin/slice` also require `mode: shared` in `/etc/positron/dice.yaml`.

new_terms.definition: The launcher scripts `bin/rinzler` and `bin/runtron`. They start the built programs `gen/rinzler` and `gen/runtron`.
The file `/etc/positron/dice.yaml`. Its `mode` key selects the host mode (`legacy` or `shared`). Its `socket` key names the socket of the Dice daemon.
The host mode in which one Dice daemon serves all users of the server. The Dice host configuration file selects it with `mode: shared`.
The host mode without a Dice daemon. It applies when the Dice host configuration file is missing or has `mode: legacy`.
The set of slots that the Dice daemon assigned to one program that it started.
The directory where the Dice daemon keeps its state file, log, lock files and the logs of the programs it starts.
The part of `config/test-benchmarks.json` that holds the benchmark data of one server type.

notes: Corrections against the input records, all taken from the code. (1) DICE_RUNTIME_DIR: with `mode: shared` the socket path comes from the host configuration and does not follow the runtime directory (socket_path in bin/dice), so the row does not list the socket among the moved files. (2) SLICE_STATE_DIR: the record said bin/slice reports an error for a per-user directory with a wrong owner or mode. write_state catches that OSError and returns, so no state file is written and nothing is printed. (3) SLICE_MANIFEST_OVERRIDE: a missing or invalid file does not end in an uncaught Python error. The handlers in bin/slice print an `error:` line and exit. (4) DICE_SLOTS: four readers parse the text differently (C++ strict, wrappers skip empty items, bin/slice and bench_refresh_quiesce.py accept ranges). The row states each. bench_refresh_quiesce.py reads it without a test of DICE_DAEMON_CHILD. (5) DICE_RUNTIME_DIR, DICE_SOCKET_PATH and DICE_STATE_PATH are in group dice-test-hooks: every daemon command raises unless the host configuration has `mode: shared`, and with `mode: shared` the overrides are refused outside the pytest override. Stale documentation seen while checking: doc/slice.md says the default of SLICE_BOX_CAPACITY is 8, the code has no such literal and reads the resource map. doc/dice.md lists DICE_BOX_SLOTS before `--box`, the code uses `--box` first (Daemon.__init__).
